flags.note: The string of participles (יֹרֵד, לָבוּשׁ) with coordinating ו mirrors Greek participial construction. Native Hebrew would more likely use finite verbs or restructure with asyndetic participles.
The temporal clause 'in the hour that he cried out' using שֶׁ is acceptable in Mishnaic Hebrew but shows possible Greek influence from ἐν ᾗ ὥρᾳ construction.
While שֶׁ temporal clauses are found in Mishnaic Hebrew, the frequency and pattern may reflect Greek μετὰ τὸ + infinitive constructions.

flags.hebrew: מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ... וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם
flags.note: The repeated 'what that is in...' construction using מה שיש closely mirrors Greek τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ/αὐτοῖς. Native Hebrew would more likely use simple construct chains or אשר clauses.
The oath content 'that there is no more time' using שֶׁ + negative existential mimics Greek ὅτι χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται. Classical Hebrew would use כי or direct speech.
The temporal clause 'when the seven angels blow' shows possible influence from Greek ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις construction, though שֶׁ is acceptable in late Hebrew.
The comparative clause 'just as he made known' using כמו שֶׁ reflects Greek καθὼς construction. Classical Hebrew would prefer כאשר or simple כ.
The use of plural imperative תנו when addressing a single angel is unusual and may reflect Greek δός μοι. Hebrew would typically use singular תן or restructure the request.
Another temporal שֶׁ clause 'after I ate' shows the pattern of frequent שֶׁ subordination that may reflect Greek influence, though individually acceptable in late Hebrew.
